note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a BOT 12, 13; A06b BOT 12, 13; L05 BOT 15(2)): ordinary naturalisation after 10 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. The Citizenship (Amendment) Act No. 23 of 2024 (published 29 October 2024) permits dual citizenship for adults, which was previously allowed only for children (Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative's summary of the Act), so a Motswana now keeps the citizenship on taking another. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Government of Botswana (Department of Immigration and Citizenship), Renunciation of Foreign Citizenship Application; Government of Botswana, Citizenship Application – Declaration of Intention (served at www.gov.bw). It confirmed birth in the territory and descent. It was silent on the years of residence, renunciation and loss on taking another citizenship, which still rest on the sources above, re-read that day and found the same, save the one that didn't answer. The government's renunciation page still tells dual citizens they lose citizenship at 21 unless they renounce, the rule before the 2024 Amendment Act; the Act itself wasn't reached, and the later source that reported it (CRAI) didn't answer on 2026-11-03 (HTTP 504 twice, no Common Crawl capture), so the file's lapses rests on that report as read on its earlier date.

sources.said: Person has been resident in Botswana for a continuous period of 12 months prior to the application, and has been resident for at least 10 out of the previous 12 years. ... n.a. ... Person is over 18 years of age and acquires citizenship of another country by voluntary and formal act. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Botswana to a citizen. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born abroad to a citizen. ... No provision ... No provision

sources.title: Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative, Botswana: Citizenship Amendment Act, No. 23 of 2024 (published 29 October 2024)
sources.said: (Cap.1.01 of the Laws of Botswana), to provide for dual citizenship to be permitted for adults (previously only allowed for children)

sources.title: Government of Botswana (Department of Immigration and Citizenship), Renunciation of Foreign Citizenship Application
sources.said: Any person who is both a citizen of Botswana and a foreign country will cease to be a citizen of Botswana unless the following measures are taken before the attainment of age twenty one (21): Renounced the citizenship of the foreign country. ... This service applies to people who are Botswana citizens by birth, descent and registration but are also citizens of other countries, and are under the age of twenty one (21) years. NB: Born in Botswana or outside Botswana and one of your parents is a citizen of Botswana at the time of your birth.

sources.title: Government of Botswana, Citizenship Application – Declaration of Intention (served at www.gov.bw)
sources.said: An applicant who intends to apply for a Certificate of Naturalization as a Foreign Spouse must submit a Declaration of Intention Form as required by the Citizenship Act. ... The applicant must be a non-citizen married to a Botswana citizen and has resided in Botswana for a minimum of two and a half years.
